question: Which business model type typically has the highest operating leverage?
before: SaaS has overwhelmingly fixed costs (engineering, cloud infra). Marginal cost per additional subscriber is near zero. 20% revenue increase can produce 40-60% profit increase. IT services scales linearly with headcount. Grocery has high variable costs.
after:
Concept: Operating leverage measures how profit changes relative to revenue changes. High operating leverage occurs when fixed costs dominate the cost structure and marginal costs are minimal — so each additional rupee of revenue flows almost entirely to the bottom line.

Why this is correct: SaaS businesses like Zoho and Freshworks have predominantly fixed costs (R&D, cloud infrastructure, customer support platforms) that don't scale with user volume. Once these costs are covered, adding a new subscriber costs almost nothing to serve — marginal cost approaches zero. This creates the steepest profit-to-revenue ratio. A 20% revenue increase can translate into 40–60% profit growth because the fixed cost base is already in place.

Why the others are wrong:

A) IT services (TCS, Infosys) scales nearly linearly with headcount and project staffing. When revenue grows 20%, costs rise almost proportionally because you must hire engineers and allocate them to client work. Operating leverage remains moderate.

C) Grocery retail (DMart) has high variable costs embedded in cost of goods sold and supply chain. Even with fixed store infrastructure, COGS remains tied directly to sales volume, limiting the profit swing from revenue growth.

D) Logistics (Delhivery) must scale fleet, warehousing, and workforce in line with shipment volume. Fixed infrastructure costs exist but variable costs (fuel, labour, packaging) rise with throughput, preventing the extreme leverage seen in pure software.

Intuition: SaaS is the extreme case of "build once, sell infinitely." An engineer writes code once; millions of users access it for ₹X per month. In contrast, services firms rent out human time (linear cost growth), and asset-heavy businesses like retail and logistics must continuously reinvest in capacity. For an equity analyst evaluating scalability and margin expansion potential, SaaS models offer the most dramatic operating leverage and therefore the highest sensitivity to revenue surprises.
